items.title: Dr. Mehmet Güllüoğlu
items.dc:creator: Elayne Wangalwa
items.content:
Dr. Mehmet Güllüoğlu
Director of the Humanitarian Sector Division and Head of OCHA in Geneva
Elayne Wangalwa 13 Nov. 2026 4.44 p.m.

Dr. Güllüoğlu is a senior diplomat and public health professional with two decades of leadership experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster management and international cooperation. He previously worked as Senior Adviser to the President of Türkiye. Before that, he served as Türkiye's Humanitarian Aid Coordinator for the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) to oversee the coordination and monitoring of Türkiye's humanitarian activities in Gaza.

From 2021 to 2024, he served as Ambassador of Türkiye to the United Republic of Tanzania. Between 2017 and 2021, he headed Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Authority, leading a nationwide structure of 81 provincial directorates, 11 response brigades, roughly 6,000 personnel, and 100,000 volunteers. In this role, he helped develop the national volunteer model that proved vital for disaster response and public awareness.

He previously served as Director General of the Turkish Red Crescent (2013–2017), where he led major humanitarian programs supporting more than three million Syrian refugees, contributed to the Emergency Social Safety Net programme assisting over 1.4 million people, and directed field operations in Bangladesh, OPT, Pakistan, Somalia, Syria and Yemen. Earlier in his career, he led health promotion and research at the Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Health, practiced emergency medicine and coordinated health projects for Doctors Worldwide in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Niger and OPT.

Dr. Güllüoğlu holds a PhD in Public Health from Istanbul University and a medical degree from Marmara University. He served as Vice Chairman of the Turkish Green Crescent (Yeşilay) and Secretary General of the International Federation of Green Crescents. He speaks English, Arabic and Swahili, in addition to his native Turkish.
